chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who died and left three hundred dirhams, and upon him was two hundred dirhams of zakat, and he bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Hajj is performed for him from the nearest [portion of the money], and whatever remains is allocated to the zakat.'
ai.seo_question: How is a deceased person's debt of zakat handled if they also bequeathed Hajj but left insufficient funds?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the priority of fulfilling a bequeathed Hajj over outstanding zakat obligations when the estate is insufficient, establishing that the pilgrimage is performed first using the nearest available funds. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that voluntary acts of worship (like Hajj) can take precedence over obligatory financial dues (zakat) in cases of limited liquidity, ensuring the deceased's spiritual debt is addressed before settling monetary liabilities.
